title: In & Out: Filling & Emptying
strapline: Fill it up, tip it out, do it again — the tireless toddler work of putting things in and taking them out.
intent: Honour one of the deepest fascinations of this age — filling a container, emptying it, and starting over without tiring.
Develop the hand skills of gathering, dropping, tipping and pouring, and the whole-body effort of carrying full containers about.
Grow the earliest ideas of quantity and capacity — how many corks the pot holds, when it is full, when it is all gone.
Support long, self-directed concentration on a task the child sets and repeats entirely for themselves.
Feed hiding-and-finding — what goes in can be lost, tipped out and found all over again.
implementation: Offer buckets, pots, bags, tins, jugs and posting boxes alongside loose fillers — corks, large pompoms, wooden pegs, pinecones, big buttons on rings — all safely sized.
Sit close and let the emptying happen; the tipping-out is not mess to be stopped but the second half of the play.
Narrate the quantity and capacity words as they surface ('the pot is full now', 'all gone — shall we fill it again?').
Watch each child's version — the poster who wants a lid with a slot, the transporter who fills a bag and hauls it away, the pourer who wants water and a jug.
Refresh fillers weekly, keep everything larger than a choke tube, and fold tidying into the game — everything back in its own container.
key_questions: How many corks can the pot hold before it spills?
Is it full yet, or is there room for more?
Where did the pompoms go when you tipped them out?
Can you carry the full bag all the way to the mat?
Shall we fill it up one more time?

impact.text: Toddlers fill containers and tip them out, again and again on purpose, loving the whole in-and-out cycle.
Children gather, drop, tip and pour, small hands growing more controlled with every fill.
Toddlers carry full bags and pots deliberately from here to there, working hard at transporting.
Early quantity words surface at the container — 'more', 'all gone', 'full', 'big one'.
A child hides a treasure in a pot, tips it out and finds it once more, delighting in the disappearing and returning.

enhancements: A posting box with a slot cut in the lid, for corks and pegs to disappear and reappear.
A water-and-jug station so filling and emptying can be done with a pourable material.
Fabric drawstring bags to fill, cinch and haul across the room.
A treasure hidden among the fillers, so every emptying holds a small find.
Wall-mounted tubes at toddler height — post at the top, catch the fillers at the bottom.

playing_exploring: Toddlers combine containers and fillers freely, filling and emptying with no fixed end.
The materials are tested with hands, ears and whole-body carrying.
active_learning: Children repeat the fill-and-tip cycle tirelessly, refining how they gather and pour each time.
The task is entirely self-set — how full, how many, how far to carry.
creating_thinking: Toddlers invent their own goals — fill the bag to the brim, hide the cork so it can't be found.
They notice what happens — the pot overflows, the bag is too heavy — and adjust.
